name: Palms Up Please
description: 🤲🥺 pairs two open, upturned hands with a wide-eyed pleading face, turning a request into an exaggerated “pretty please” that can be sweet, needy, or playful.
meaning: The cupped palms ask for something while 🥺 supplies the puppy-dog eyes, so together they mean “please, give me what I want” with more charm and pressure than either image gives alone. The tone can be sincere, flirtatious, apologetic, or silly.
examples: can you send me the address again? 🤲🥺
one more bite and i’ll behave 🤲🥺
please let me stay up past midnight 🤲🥺
can i have the last slice? 🤲🥺
seoDescription: What does 🤲🥺 mean? It’s an exaggerated “pretty please”: open hands ask for something while pleading puppy eyes add needy, playful pressure.

longForm.overview:
🤲 shows two bare palms held upward, like someone is offering, receiving, or asking for a favor. 🥺 adds huge shiny eyes and lifted brows, the face people use when begging or acting helplessly cute. Put together, they create one clear picture: the sender is holding out both hands and asking for something with the most pleading expression possible. The hands make the request; the face makes it emotionally irresistible.

In practice, 🤲🥺 is a “pretty please” with attitude. A friend might use it for a snack, an extra turn at a game, or one more episode; a romantic partner might use it after “come over?”; someone at work might ask a coworker to cover a small task. Because the images are so exaggerated, the combo can turn a mild request into a joke without sounding harsh. It can also show vulnerability: “please don’t be mad” or “i miss you” becomes warmer and less confrontational when the pleading face is doing the apologizing.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🤲🥺 shows up when someone wants a small yes: an extension, a favor, another serving, or forgiveness. It works especially well when the request is personal but not serious, because the palms look hopeful and 🥺 adds comic insistence. “one more episode?” and “can you check my answer?” both get the same exaggerated please.

Friends use it to nag playfully about food, plans, and attention. Dating chats use it as soft flirtation or reassurance, especially after asking to see someone or saying they miss them. At work, use it for low-stakes requests between colleagues who joke with each other; during a deadline, it may look unserious.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Don’t use 🤲🥺 to pressure someone into giving you something they have already refused. The puppy eyes can make persistence look cute, but repeated pleading may feel manipulative. If you need time off, money, a commitment, or actual help, state the request plainly and let the other person decide.

It also sits badly after a serious mistake. “please don’t be angry” is not an apology, and adding 🤲🥺 cannot replace an explanation, accountability, or repair. In a customer chat, an urgent request, or a sensitive family disagreement, use clear words and leave room for a real answer.
longForm.howToReply:
Reply in kind when the request is playful. If someone asks for the last slice with 🤲🥺, you can tease them, offer a smaller yes, or say “you’re already using both hands to beg.” Match the cuteness without pretending the underlying request deserves no boundary. A clear “only if you replace the toilet paper” keeps the joke moving.

If the sender is asking for reassurance or forgiveness, notice that before matching the joke. “of course” or “you’re not in trouble” answers what the pleading face may be reaching for. If it lands on your post, react to the request: ask what they want, set a limit, or say yes plainly.

faqs.question: What does 🤲🥺 mean in a group chat?
faqs.answer: It is an exaggerated “pretty please”: 🤲 asks or offers, while 🥺 adds needy puppy eyes. In a group chat, it usually works as a playful request for food, attention, or one small favor.

faqs.question: Is 🤲🥺 flirty?
faqs.answer: It can be, especially in a dating chat, because the pleading face adds vulnerability and the upturned hands can suggest “come here” or “give me your attention.” The same combo is also common among friends asking for something silly, so context decides.

faqs.question: Does 🤲🥺 mean thank you?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. 🤲 can be an open-handed offer or gratitude gesture, but 🥺 turns the picture toward begging or wanting, so people usually read the pair as a request rather than a thank-you.

faqs.question: Can I use 🤲🥺 at work?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a low-stakes request to a coworker you already know well. Avoid it for deadlines, discipline, money, or any situation where the plain wording needs to be taken seriously.

conversationExamples.message: can you take a quick look at my slide before standup? i fixed the typo this time 🤲🥺
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a light request for help under a real deadline, softened by the emoji. Respond with the specific time you can review it instead of answering only with teasing.

conversationExamples.message: the pizza place says one slice left and i’m already there 🤲🥺
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender wants the group to help decide whether to claim the final slice. Tell them to grab it or order another pizza rather than leaving the request hanging.

conversationExamples.message: come over and hold me? it’s been a long day 🤲🥺
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is vulnerable and flirtatious, asking for affection as much as company. Confirm whether you can actually see them and answer the invitation directly.

conversationExamples.message: mom, can i have the last pancake? i’ll make coffee 🤲🥺
conversationExamples.interpretation: A familiar family request for the last breakfast food, made cute with the combo. A parent can say yes, offer a trade, or save it for tomorrow.

conversationExamples.message: can you screenshot the ticket code before it disappears? i’m panicking a little 🤲🥺
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender may need the code immediately, so send the screenshot or explain where to find it. The playful emoji should not delay the practical help.
